Ok, I discovered this when I was trying to figure out a way to have a semi-sweet/semi-dry cider that didn't take using a super-finicky yeast and would let me drink my ciders sooner than 6 months from when I "brewed" them.

I give you Stupid Easy Cider!

Ingredients: 5-5.5 gallons preservative free apple juice--store brand is fine, but sure--Green Market Cider is better. I usually go with whatever's on sale at my local grocery store for $2/half gallon.

Yeast

Process: Pour 4-4.5 gallons of juice into a clean and sanitized fermentor. I like to pour half a jug, then shake the hell out of the rest of the jug to at least give a nod towards aeration. Pitch the yeast--I've had great results with quite a wide variety of yeasts, but I like S-33 because it's cheap and does a great job. You can rehydrate if you want, but remember--this is supposed to be stupid easy. ;)

Let it ferment out until it drops clear. This may take 4-6 weeks, just be patient.

Once the juice has fermented into cider and dropped clear, rack it onto a gallon of juice. I keg, so I purge the keg, pour the juice in, then rack the cider on top of it, stopping the racking when I reach 5 gallons. If you're bottling, rack onto the juice in the bottling bucket.

If you keg, fridge the cider and put it on co2. It's ready to drink as soon as it's carbed, and it's delicious. If you bottle, it's a bit more of a pain. Let the cider go until it reaches almost the level of carb you like (a lot of people like to use a single PET soda bottle to monitor the carb level), then fridge the whole batch. Alternatively, you can bottle pasteurize, but it's not for the faint of heart.

After a couple of days in the fridge, the cider is ready to drink. Just don't let it get warm for long, or fermentation WILL start back up again.
Simple, stupid easy cider that comes out great every time. Works best with kegging. Xpost v/Cider

A couple of factoids about English aircraft production.
One: The largest Cryolite mine (Cryolite is necessary for the refining of aluminum) was in Lviguit Greenland (a territory of Denmark) With the Danish government under the control of NAZI Germany the Germans had access to the Cryolite for their Aluminum production. The Local sheriffs of Greenland formed a defacto independent neutral state, that the United State under the provisions of the Monroe doctrine recognized their Neutrality and envorced that Neutralilty on 4 May by the appearence of Two US Coast Guard Cutters to support a Neutral Greenland.

Second point. The Spitfire was not really all that superior to the BF109, while it could out turn a BF-109 It could not climb as fast or go inverted. It wasn't until the fitting of the Bendix Stromberg Pressure Carburetor to the Rolls Royce Merlin engine that allowed it to operate inverted and the availability of 115/145 Octain Gasoline that the spitfire came into its own. However the Spitfire was inferior in almost every aspect to the Japanese Zero Untill late in the war. The main problem with the Spitfire is that it used the RAF48 Airfoil which had its maximum dynamic pressure at 30% to 40% of cord. The RAF 48 Airfoil had a relative flat bottom so the air traveling under the wing traveled at a much lower velocity of the air traveling over the top of the wing. The result of this difference of velocity caused the Spitfire wing to stall at a much higher speed than the laminar flow airfoil of the BF-109 (and the same airfoil on the P-51) However the Spitfire was a much a much easier plane to fly as the stalls were gentile and gave plenty of warning. The stalls of the BF-109 and P-51 were rapid and vicious with little or no warning when the lift was going to break loose. The vicious stalls were partly offset by the wash in at the wing tips that caused the root of the wing to stall while the tip of the wing kept flying and having control of the ailerons. The 115/145 Octain avgas allowed the engine to run at a much higher manifold pressure (Yielding additional horsepower) than the DB-601 of the BF109.

This is the top post of all time in /r/Canada. I think that people are willing to upvote it because they have experienced similar issues with Canada Post. Personally, I would jump on the bandwagon if I saw a video of the worker leaving the parcel like that. For people who don't want to go over there, here's OP's comment in the original post.

I'm sure this (the courier being a lazy shit) has been the case for some time. In the past, I did complain, but the real problem has been in dealing with the Canada Post bureaucracy. Online tracking for two of the packages showed that they had been delivered, and as a result I was unable to dispute that through their website. I called to speak to someone about it, and the response from the person at the call centre was that I had to contact the companies that had shipped the packages and ask them to contact Canada Post to request an investigation into the incidents be opened. For the third package, which had been sent from the US, I was told that the person who had sent it to me had to go to his local post office to ask the USPS to do the same thing (ask Canada Post to open an investigation re the missing package). After several weeks, a few things happened: I received a couple of odd email messages about only one of the missing packages that asked me to confirm whether I had given them the correct address, and I got a couple of phone calls asking whether the packages had ever been delivered. I did speak to a person at my post office and she told me that they had been receiving complaints about mail delivery in the area every day. And when she went the extra mile and tried to call someone who might be able to help me, she ended up with the same people / same call centre that I had spoken to in the first place.

Would the proposed solution to this be: "well use a private courier to deliver it right to your door then?"

Aside from the fact that private couriers do the exact same thing with regards to leaving your parcel wherever, my primary issue with that line of privatized thought is there are certain communities that the private couriers will NOT deliver to. Where I currently live the option is Canada Post or nothing. Fedex, Purolator, and UPS do not service my community. I enjoy our quaint little TWO employee Post Office here in town where each of the residents has their own PO box inside the Post Office. If a parcel arrives for us, a notice is left in our PO box to take to the service counter where a Canada Post employee will then retrieve the parcel from their back storage area. Easy, secure, and logical. Canada Post gets it to the community, the residents visit the Post Office to retrieve their stuff. It's so bloody simple it boggles the mind that anyone wasted brain power suggesting these silly brown pop up mail boxes were the solution 2-3 decades ago.

When we first moved to this little community I was a little disgruntled that Canada Post was the only option, but now I see it as the premium option. If I'm not home or able to check my mail I feel my items are more secure safe inside the Post Office than being left under our door mat or bouncing around endlessly in the back of a private courier as they relentlessly try to deliver it to the front door.

To me it's simple. Either your community is large enough to warrant door to door delivery from a properly trained Canada Post employee OR you get an old fashioned and functional post office to visit at your leisure.

I live just outside of a small town with a post office. I get my mail delivered to one of those mail boxes at the end of my street. If I have a package that is too large for the parcel box I have two options. Option 1 -They leave a pick-up card in my mailbox and I wait until the weekend to pick it up. Monday to Friday, they are open at 8:30 to 5:00 and closed 11:45 to 1:15 for lunch. This makes it difficult to pick up anything during the week. Saturday they are open 9:00-12:00. Option 2 - The leave it on my from door step, regardless of the weather. I came home last winter to find a package on my front step buried under 6cm of snow. When I called the post office to ask why, they replied it was the policy if no signature was required. I'm past the point of thinking Canada Post even cares anymore. I believe even they know they are close to being irrelevant.
